correctness.rationale: For every positive diagonal P in the nondominant regime, the polygonal Gram certificate H with Hu=0 establishes lambda_max >= S(1+S)/W and lambda_min <= S/W for the same W, giving kappa >= 1+S, attained by P=I. In the dominant regime, restriction to the coordinate j and residual vector yields a 2x2 correlation rho whose optimal diagonally scaled condition number is (1+rho)/(1-rho). The exhibited one-entry scaling attains it because the other full-space eigenvalues equal 1 and lie between the two planar extremes exactly when M>R. R=0 and S=0 are explicit. The exact symbolic and numerical tests from verify.py were replayed from the same package; they complement rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: The result solves a natural high-dimensional diagonal SPD spectral-conditioning problem in an exact closed form, identifies the precise no-scaling-versus-one-coordinate transition for spiked matrices, and provides a structural dual certificate for global optimality against all asymmetries. It also gives an exact explicit case in which Jacobi diagonal normalization worsens the condition number; it is a meaningful theoretical test family for diagonal preconditioning, without claiming convergence gains beyond spectral conditioning.
